media_work.focus_or_theme: False confessions, police deception, wrongful convictions.
media_work.summaryNotes: Case involved police falsely telling suspect his father implicated him.

media_item.focus_or_theme: False confession induced by police deception/fabrication in the Martin Tankleff case.
media_item.summary_notes: Examines how police convinced Martin Tankleff his father implicated him (a fabrication), leading to a false confession. The police tactic of lying about evidence to secure a confession is the central element.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Examines how police convinced Tankleff his father implicated him (a fabrication) leading to false confession. Available via ABC.
research_notes_other.research_findings: Searches did not confirm a specific 20/20 episode with this title. However, the details precisely match the well-known Martin Tankleff case. CBS's 48 Hours program covered the case. The police tactic of lying about evidence (the father's "statement") to secure a confession is the central, unique element of this case.

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Murder (of parents, Seymour and Arlene Tankleff)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Wrongfully convicted of murdering his parents based on a coerced false confession. Police falsely claimed his father implicated him before dying. He was exonerated after serving over 17 years and settled a civil lawsuit.
contributing_factors_raw: Coerced false confession (obtained after police falsely claimed his father, before dying, implicated him)
Ignoring evidence pointing to other suspects
